metaDescription: A local desktop writing environment. Every decision in it answers one question: will this interrupt the person writing?
ogTitle: ZenMD — a writing environment that never interrupts you
ogDescription: Nothing interrupts you while you write.
lede: ZenMD is a local desktop writing environment. Every decision in it answers one question — will this interrupt the person writing? It was built for Chinese, where getting that wrong is loudest, and it holds for whatever else you write.
heroAlt: ZenMD in zen mode: the sidebar, the article list and the preview are all dismissed, leaving only the piece being written
heroCaption: This is zen mode. Sidebar, list and preview all step aside, leaving the piece you are writing — and one button to bring them back.
refusalsH2: Focus is not a tidier interface. It is the absence of interruptions.
refusalsIntro: Every editor claims to be distraction free, and usually means the chrome is minimal. ZenMD is after something else: in the few seconds while you are typing, what is able to interrupt? Which is why its spec carries a long list of things it deliberately refuses to do — each one a habit other editors have that no writer ever asked for.
r1a: Pressing Tab to indent a line
r1b: It will not throw your cursor at some button. Tab only indents
r2b: It will not pop up to guess at your word. There is no autocomplete
r3b: It will not put a line of YAML in front of you. Metadata is filled in once, then gone
r4a: Summoning a snippet and changing your mind
r4b: It will not leave behind anything for you to clean up
r5a: Reading the candidate list, choosing a character
r5b: It will not autosave before you have picked one
r6a: Looking for something to write about
r6b: It will not hand you a graph to wander around in for an hour instead
shotsH2: Everything is there when you want it
shotsIntro: Restraint is not the same as bare. Zen mode is a switch, not the only shape.
shot1H: Write on one side, watch it become the finished thing on the other
shot1P: Markdown source on the left, rendered on the right, moving as you type. Three arrangements, one key each, and it remembers which one you left it in.
shot1Alt: The full ZenMD window: workspaces, statuses and tags on the left, the article list in the middle, the editor and live preview side by side on the right
shot2H: Type / and the shape you want falls in
shot2P: Headings, links, images, tables, task items. The cursor lands on the first thing to fill in, so you just type. Type / mid-character-selection and nothing happens — that keystroke belongs to the input method.
shot2Alt: The snippet menu opened by typing a slash in the editor, listing H1 through H6, Link, Image, Table and Checkbox
shot3H: Four themes, following the system or picked yourself
shot3P: Light, dark, forest, zen. Down to every colour in the snippet menu.
shot3Alt: ZenMD with the zen theme applied, the whole window turned to a warm paper tone
signupH2: The app is free. Only the hosted parts are paid.
signupIntro: Everything you do locally is free and unmetered — your files are on your own disk, and there is no reason for me to charge you for that. What costs money is the part that needs a server kept running.
tierFree2: No cap on pieces or workspaces
tierFree3: Four themes, snippet menu, paste an image
tierFree4: Your files stay yours — leave any time
tierPaidAnnual: or $50 a year — ten months' worth
tierPaid3: Publish a piece to a link anyone can open
tierQuote: "The paragraph I deleted three weeks ago — I can get it back."
tierSoon:
Sync and publishing are still being built.
You will not be charged a cent before they ship.
formSubmit: Tell me when I can download it
formCheckbox: Tell me when sync and publishing ship too — I would pay for those.
formWantsLabel: The one feature you want most?
formWantsPlaceholder: e.g. full-text search, a Windows build, export to PDF…
formPlatform: Right now this is macOS on Apple Silicon only — if you are on something else, say so in the box above. I am counting who is waiting.
formPromise: Two emails, ever: "you can download it" and "the hosted parts are live". No newsletter, nothing passed on to anyone, and replying to say stop removes you.
formDone: Got it. I will write when you can download it.
